title: Estimated acquisition cost per million voxels — optical and EM

rows.label: ExM + confocalOptical
rows.note: Compiling molecular ultrastructure into neural dynamics — arXiv:2603.25713v1, Table A1 (p. 18) ↗Many of these numbers come from a crowdsourcing effort: we thank the many involved scientists for providing estimates of these numbers. No claim beyond rough size (order of magnitude) is made.Table A1 row 1: ExM + Confocal; Approx. Voxels/$ = 1,000,000,000. Published Table A1 efficiency. Table says Total Cost ($/h), but composition/amortization/utilization/labor/maintenance and price-year are unspecified. Coverage of tissue preparation, reconstruction, storage and proofreading costs is unverified. Cost and throughput are crowdsourced estimates. Effective optical resolution in Chen et al. (2015), not a recorded voxel sampling for the cost estimate. Display conversion: 0.001 $/million voxels.

rows.label: Single-beam SEMElectron microscopy
rows.note: Compiling molecular ultrastructure into neural dynamics — arXiv:2603.25713v1, Table A1 (p. 18) ↗Many of these numbers come from a crowdsourcing effort: we thank the many involved scientists for providing estimates of these numbers. No claim beyond rough size (order of magnitude) is made.Table A1 row 3: EM (SEM, single beam); Approx. Voxels/$ = 100,000,000. Published Table A1 efficiency. Table says Total Cost ($/h), but composition/amortization/utilization/labor/maintenance and price-year are unspecified. Coverage of tissue preparation, reconstruction, storage and proofreading costs is unverified. 2018 is the table year, not a verified first-demonstration year. Do not label this SBFSEM2004. Not specified in Table A1. Its reference 55 is Hughes et al. 2014, not Denk & Horstmann 2004. Display conversion: 0.01 $/million voxels.

rows.label: ExLLSMOptical
rows.note: Compiling molecular ultrastructure into neural dynamics — arXiv:2603.25713v1, Table A1 (p. 18) ↗Many of these numbers come from a crowdsourcing effort: we thank the many involved scientists for providing estimates of these numbers. No claim beyond rough size (order of magnitude) is made.Table A1 row 4: ExLLSM; Approx. Voxels/$ = 1,000,000,000. Published Table A1 efficiency. Table says Total Cost ($/h), but composition/amortization/utilization/labor/maintenance and price-year are unspecified. Coverage of tissue preparation, reconstruction, storage and proofreading costs is unverified. Primary acquisition rate 10–100 million voxels/s; dollar efficiency remains author estimate. Effective optical resolution at 4x expansion; primary paper separately describes ~30–50 nm voxel dimensions. Display conversion: 0.001 $/million voxels.

rows.label: ExA-SPIM 2023Optical
rows.note: Compiling molecular ultrastructure into neural dynamics — arXiv:2603.25713v1, Table A1 (p. 18) ↗Many of these numbers come from a crowdsourcing effort: we thank the many involved scientists for providing estimates of these numbers. No claim beyond rough size (order of magnitude) is made.Table A1 row 5: ExA-SPIM (LSFM); Approx. Voxels/$ = 10,000,000,000. Published Table A1 efficiency. Table says Total Cost ($/h), but composition/amortization/utilization/labor/maintenance and price-year are unspecified. Coverage of tissue preparation, reconstruction, storage and proofreading costs is unverified. 2023 preprint; final version published 2025. Preserve table year. Primary maximum 946 Mvox/s in final version, not the table’s 1e12 vox/h. Context from final eLife version (2025), effective optical resolution with 4x expansion; not guaranteed to describe the exact 2023 cost-estimate setting. Display conversion: 0.0001 $/million voxels.

rows.label: MultiSEM 506Electron microscopy
rows.note: Compiling molecular ultrastructure into neural dynamics — arXiv:2603.25713v1, Table A1 (p. 18) ↗Many of these numbers come from a crowdsourcing effort: we thank the many involved scientists for providing estimates of these numbers. No claim beyond rough size (order of magnitude) is made.Table A1 row 6: EM (Zeiss, MultiSEM 506); Approx. Voxels/$ = 1,000,000,000. Published Table A1 efficiency. Table says Total Cost ($/h), but composition/amortization/utilization/labor/maintenance and price-year are unspecified. Coverage of tissue preparation, reconstruction, storage and proofreading costs is unverified. 91 beams, not 61 (505 has 61). Cost-normalization arithmetic does not equal the rounded stated vox/$; retain stated value. Example voxel sampling from ZEISS brochure (4 nm pixels, 50 nm section), not resolution specified by Table A1. Display conversion: 0.001 $/million voxels.

rows.label: MultiSEM 706Electron microscopy
rows.note: Compiling molecular ultrastructure into neural dynamics — arXiv:2603.25713v1, Table A1 (p. 18) ↗Many of these numbers come from a crowdsourcing effort: we thank the many involved scientists for providing estimates of these numbers. No claim beyond rough size (order of magnitude) is made.Table A1 row 7: EM (Zeiss, MultiSEM 706); Approx. Voxels/$ = 1,000,000,000. Published Table A1 efficiency. rows.label: mesoSPIMOptical
rows.note: Compiling molecular ultrastructure into neural dynamics — arXiv:2603.25713v1, Table A1 (p. 18) ↗Many of these numbers come from a crowdsourcing effort: we thank the many involved scientists for providing estimates of these numbers. rows.label: PEEM*PEEM · prospective
rows.note: Compiling molecular ultrastructure into neural dynamics — arXiv:2603.25713v1, Table A1 (p. 18) ↗Many of these numbers come from a crowdsourcing effort: we thank the many involved scientists for providing estimates of these numbers. No claim beyond rough size (order of magnitude) is made.Table A1 row 10: PEEM; Approx. Voxels/$ = 20,000,000,000. Published Table A1 efficiency. Table says Total Cost ($/h), but composition/amortization/utilization/labor/maintenance and price-year are unspecified. Coverage of tissue preparation, reconstruction, storage and proofreading costs is unverified. Table uses 2024, cited PNAS publication is 2025. ~2 Gvox/s net scenario is prospective; do not present 2e10 vox/$ as measured end-to-end performance. Primary paper demonstrates synaptic-resolution PEEM and faster imaging at coarser resolution; the 8x8x30 nm setting in its mouse-brain estimate is prospective, not matched demonstrated high-speed acquisition. Display conversion: 0.00005 $/million voxels.
